Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today - the dedicated routing and prefix caching looked promising. A few follow-ups from our engineering team around authentication and key management:

- We currently use a mix of API keys for backend services and OAuth 2.0 for our external partner flows. How does Redwood recommend mapping those patterns to your API (API keys vs service accounts vs JWT/OIDC)?
- Key rotation - we have quarterly rotation requirements and need to avoid rolling restarts for live inference. Any best practices or built-in support?
- For server-to-server calls (our microservices calling Redwood), do you recommend short-lived JWTs via a service account or long-lived API keys scoped to a project?
- We also want to enable embeddings/reranking for search. Any auth implications (scopes, rate limits) we should design for?

Attaching our internal SSO and key management doc for context (paymentsco_sso_requirements.pdf). Can we get a short architecture recommendation that we can present to our security team?

Hi Alex - really useful questions, thanks for sending the doc. High-level answers up front, then Dev added a short architecture sketch and operational notes below.

High level recommendation (TL;DR):
- For server-to-server (internal microservices): use short-lived JWTs issued by your identity provider (service account flow) with audience scoped to Redwood. We support OIDC/JWT verification and can accept tokens via standard Authorization: Bearer.
- For partner/external flows: keep OAuth/OIDC for user-facing flows; Redwood can accept downstream-on-behalf-of tokens or you can mint scoped API keys for partner integrations where a user context is not required.
- For admin/ops tasks (key issuance, provisioning): use role-scoped API keys with limited privileges and rotate them frequently; pair with RBAC in your sidecar.
- Key rotation: Redwood supports seamless key rotation via overlapping key windows (we validate new keys while accepting the previous for a configurable TTL). No inference node restarts required.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Dev to share a concise architecture diagram (service account + token flow + optional API key fallback).
2) We'll share a short playbook on rotation windows and recommended TTLs.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call with your security team next week to walk the diagram and answers.

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Alex - quick technical sketch attached (paymentsco_authn_architecture_v2.png). Key points and config snippets below.

1) Recommended flows:
- Internal server-to-server:
  - Create a PaymentsCo service account in your IdP (SAML/OIDC).
  - Issue short-lived JWTs (5-15m) with aud claim set to redwood-inference and scope to the model access required (e.g., embeddings:read, generate:write).
  - Redwood validates JWTs via your IdP jwks endpoint.
- Long-running worker processes: use a local short-lived token refresher that exchanges a long-lived service key for short-lived tokens - avoids embedding long-lived credentials in containers.
- External partner flows:
  - For partner API clients where user context is absent, use scoped API keys tied to a specific project and route. We support tag-based RBAC and per-key rate limits in the console.

2) Key rotation and overlap windows:
- We recommend a rotation window pattern: publish new key, enable both old+new for a 48h overlap, then deprecate old key after verification. Redwood's token verifier supports key id (kid) lookup and will accept keys in the overlap window.
- For JWTs, rotate signing keys at the IdP level and keep jwks cached with TTL; Redwood refreshes keys on jwks TTL expiry or 401 triggers.

3) Embeddings / reranker implications:
- Scopes: use a dedicated scope (embeddings:write, embeddings:query, rerank:invoke).
- Rate limiting: embeddings can be batched; recommend a separate key/route for embedding jobs.
- Audit logs: enable per-key audit logs to tie embedding calls back to caller identities. Redwood streams key-level usage to your S3/BigQuery for compliance if required.

4) Example header (JWT):
Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
iss: https://idp.paymentsco.com
aud: redwood-inference
scope: embeddings:query generate:write

5) Attachments: architecture diagram + an internal rotation playbook (redwood_key_rotation_playbook.docx).

If useful, we can also provide a short sample SDK snippet (Node/Python) to show token exchange and call patterns.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa & Dev - this is really helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our security review:

- For the service account JWT approach, we prefer 15-minute tokens. Is there guidance on clock skew handling and replay protection?
- For API keys used by partners: can keys be scoped to allow embeddings but not generation? We want to permit lower-cost embedding calls for third parties without exposing generate endpoints.
- Can Redwood provide an export of per-key audit logs to our SIEM (we use Splunk)?

Assuming positive answers, we're happy to book the security deep-dive next Tuesday (2027-10-26). Could you send a calendar invite?

Priya - all good questions. Short answers below, and we'll cover details in the call. I'll send a calendar invite for Tuesday 2027-10-26 10:00am PT.

- 15-minute tokens: supported. We recommend 15m tokens with a 30s clock skew tolerance. For replay protection, Redwood supports one-time nonces for high-value calls and replay detection for token ids (jti) if you want to enable it at the route level.
- Scoped API keys: yes - you can define precise scopes so partner keys grant embeddings:query but not generate:write. You can also assign per-key rate limits and cost-center tags.
- Audit log export: yes - per-key audit logs can be streamed to your Splunk/Logstash endpoint or sent to S3/GCS/BigQuery. We'll include the delivery config in the playbook.

Action items / next steps:
1) I'll send the calendar invite for 2027-10-26 10:00am PT (30m) and attach the architecture diagram + rotation playbook.
2) Dev will prepare a short SDK snippet (Node + Python) and a sample jwks configuration for your IdP.
3) Neha will follow up on pricing for dedicated routing and embedding throughput options related to this integration.

Thanks - looking forward to the call.

Best,
